name: lindel
description: Linearize multi-dimensional numeric arrays via Hilbert and Morton (Z-order) space-filling curves. Use as ORDER BY when writing Parquet to enable row-group skipping on multi-column predicates — the same Z-Order / Hilbert-Order optimization Databricks pioneered for Delta Lake.

cta.title: Z-Order / Hilbert-Order Your Parquet
cta.description: Install Lindel to encode multi-dimensional values as a single sortable integer — reorder rows in Parquet so multi-column predicates skip irrelevant row groups.

quickStart.title: Encode a multi-dimensional point to one sortable integer
quickStart.sql:
-- Hilbert keeps N-dimensional neighbors close in the 1-D ordering
SELECT hilbert_encode([10, 20]::UINTEGER[2]) AS hilbert;

quickStart.title: Order rows by the curve — this is the Parquet write-time sort key
quickStart.sql:
-- Neighbors in (x, y) end up adjacent. Wrap this SELECT in
--   COPY (...) TO 'out.parquet' (FORMAT PARQUET)
-- to persist the layout for multi-column row-group skipping.
SELECT x, y, hilbert_encode([x, y]::UINTEGER[2]) AS hilbert
FROM (VALUES (3, 5), (1, 1), (7, 0), (2, 6), (5, 3), (0, 4)) AS t(x, y)
ORDER BY hilbert;

quickStart.title: Morton (Z-order) is cheaper to compute, with weaker locality
